title: Functorial Cartan--Eilenberg resolutions and filtered total complexes
statement: Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an exact additive functor between abelian categories [def-sp-abelian]. For a bounded-below complex $K^\bullet$ in an abelian category, with $Z^q=\operatorname{Ker}(d_K^q)$, $B^{q+1}=\operatorname{Im}(d_K^q)$ and $H^q(K^\bullet)=Z^q/\operatorname{Im}(d_K^{q-1})$, a *Cartan--Eilenberg resolution* of $K^\bullet$ is a double complex $I^{\bullet,\bullet}$ [def-sp-double-complex-total], with differentials $d_I:I^{p,q}\to I^{p+1,q}$ and $d_{II}:I^{p,q}\to I^{p,q+1}$, together with a morphism of complexes $\epsilon:K^\bullet\to I^{0,\bullet}$, such that: (1) there is $i$ with $I^{p,q}=0$ for all $q<i$ and all $p$; (2) $I^{p,q}=0$ for $p<0$; (3) for each $q$ the row $(I^{\bullet,q},d_I)$, augmented by $\epsilon^q$, is an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of $K^q$; (4) for each $q$ the complex $\operatorname{Ker}(d_{II}:I^{\bullet,q}\to I^{\bullet,q+1})$ is an injective resolution of $Z^q$; (5) for each $q$ the complex $\operatorname{Im}(d_{II}:I^{\bullet,q}\to I^{\bullet,q+1})$ is an injective resolution of $B^{q+1}$; (6) for each $q$ the complex $H^q_{II}(I^{\bullet,\bullet})$ is an injective resolution of $H^q(K^\bullet)$. Let $K^\bullet$ be a bounded-below complex in $\mathcal A$ and $L^\bullet$ a bounded-below complex in $\mathcal B$, let $u:F(K^\bullet)\to L^\bullet$ be a morphism of complexes, and let $(I_K,\epsilon_K)$ and $(J_L,\epsilon_L)$ be Cartan--Eilenberg resolutions of $K^\bullet$ and $L^\bullet$. Then there is a morphism of double complexes $\phi:F(I_K)\to J_L$ with $\phi\circ F(\epsilon_K)=\epsilon_L\circ u$; in particular for each $q$ its $q$-th row $F(I_K^{\bullet,q})\to J_L^{\bullet,q}$ is a morphism of complexes compatible, through the augmentations, with $u^q:F(K^q)\to L^q$. On total complexes (defined by the formula of [def-sp-double-complex-total], the sums $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}$ being finite by (1) and (2)), filtered by the second degree $q$ (the filtration ${}''F$ of [def-sp-double-complex-total], a decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration]), $\operatorname{Tot}(\phi):\operatorname{Tot}F(I_K)\to\operatorname{Tot}J_L$ is a morphism of filtered complexes.
